ISS-03 (Issaquah PWProjectsCurrentYearConstructionPublic, DIRECT_API, VERIFIED, MVP - a live geometry query found a real on-route project, 'East Lake Sammamish Pkwy Drainage Improvement Project,' SE 51st St and ELSP). ISS-04 (Issaquah Active_Projects_gc, DIRECT_API, VERIFIED, SECONDARY - broader development-permit database, on-route relevance not yet confirmed). SAM-03 (Sammamish Transportation/TCIP_Projects, DIRECT_API, VERIFIED, SECONDARY - 22 real capital-improvement-project records, slower-moving multi-year projects). sources.research_notes:
Fetched directly during this research cycle (2026-07-28). Page renders with descriptive trail content; King County Parks confirmed via search as the agency using this page family to post active trail-alert banners (confirmed on the sibling East Lake Sammamish Trail page, see KC-03). No RSS/JSON alternative found on this page. RE-FETCHED again 2026-07-28 (third follow-up cycle, Test 21): no active alert banner was present at this fetch time - the page currently renders only standard trail description content ('About the Trail', quick facts, related topics). This is a real state change, not a contradiction: alert banners on this page family are confirmed transient, appearing and disappearing as real closure conditions change (KC-03's closure remained active on the same re-fetch pass, see below). Proposed extraction approach: the alert, when present, renders as a plain `

` heading immediately followed by one or more `

` paragraphs - not inside a semantic `

` or dedicated CSS component (confirmed by direct inspection of KC-03's live alert this cycle). There is no stable per-alert anchor/URL when no alert exists, and no confirmed machine-parseable date microformat - dates appear in prose (e.g. 'June 1, 2026'). A scraper should diff the page's heading+paragraph content block against a stored last-known-good value and flag any change for manual review, rather than trying to parse a fixed date field.

sources.research_notes:
Directly fetched 2026-07-28. Confirmed a live, dated closure alert: East Lake Sammamish Trail closed between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd, starting June 1 2026 through end of 2026, no detour, culvert replacement/salmon habitat work (George Davis Creek). This closure directly intersects the canonical route (ELST - Redmond/Sammamish segment). Cross-checked against unofficial Seattle Bike Blog coverage and City of Sammamish construction-projects page (SAM-01), consistent across all three. RE-FETCHED 2026-07-28 (third follow-up cycle, Test 21): closure notice confirmed still live and unchanged. Structure is an `

` heading ('ELST closure starting June 1, 2026') followed by `

` paragraphs - not a semantic alert/role component. Verbatim: 'A section of the East Lake Sammamish Trail will be closed starting June 1, 2026 and last through the rest of the year so crews can replace aging culverts,' with location detail 'The 600 ft trail closure area is located between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd.' Date format is prose Month-Day-Year. An in-page anchor `#elst-closure-anchor-link` was observed on the heading's link, but there is no dedicated, independently-fetchable subpage or persistent alert-specific URL - the anchor only jumps within this same page. Proposed extraction approach: fetch the full page, locate the heading matching a pattern like ' closure starting ' or containing keywords 'closure'/'closed'/'detour', capture the immediately following paragraph(s) as the alert body, and diff against the last-known-good text to detect new/changed/resolved closures.

sources.route_impact_filtering_method: direct_geometry_intersection using a corridor buffer (e.g. 100-200m) around the canonical GPX line, NOT a bounding-box query - CONFIRMED THIS CYCLE that bbox-only filtering is unreliable here: a bounding-box query against this exact route's bbox returned 1 record ('NE 165th St between 179th Pl NE and 183rd Pl NE,' Cottage Lake), which is a real active closure but geographically nowhere near the actual trail corridor - it merely falls inside the rectangular bbox. A true line-buffer intersection is required to avoid false-positive CONFIRMED_ROUTE_IMPACT classifications from this source.
sources.manual_review_requirement: Recommended for any record returned by a corridor-buffer query, to confirm the closure is genuinely on or crossing the route and not merely nearby
sources.research_notes: NEW SOURCE, added and directly live-tested in the fourth follow-up cycle (2026-07-28), discovered by querying King County's raw ArcGIS Server REST root (gismaps.kingcounty.gov/arcgis/rest/services?f=json) directly with curl rather than going through the JS-blocked opendata.arcgis.com portal (KC-05). The root services directory lists 31 folders including 'RoadAlerts' and 'Parks'; the RoadAlerts folder contains KingCo_Road_Alerts (this source), plus KingCo_Bridges, KingCo_Traffic_Cameras, and a GPServer travel-alerts tool. Live-queried KingCo_Road_Alerts/MapServer/0 (Travel Alerts layer): returned a valid ArcGIS service JSON with 34+ real fields (ClosureSegment + CurrentClosures_View schema) and 24 real active records with genuine closure names, communities, dates, and reasons (e.g. 'SE Mud Mountain Road...,' Enumclaw; 'Renton Ave S...,' Skyway; 'NE 165th St...,' Cottage Lake). This is unambiguously a real, live, unauthenticated DIRECT_API - qualitatively better data quality (structured fields, real geometry, real dates) than any STRUCTURED_WEBPAGE source in this registry. HOWEVER: its practical value to THIS route is limited by scope, not data quality - the service explicitly and only covers unincorporated King County roads, and this route runs almost entirely through incorporated cities (Seattle, Kenmore, Bothell, Woodinville, Redmond, Sammamish, Issaquah). A bbox intersection test against the route's own bounding box returned exactly 1 of 24 records, and that record (Cottage Lake) is not actually on or near the trail corridor - it is a coincidental bbox hit, confirming that this source requires true geometry-corridor filtering, not simple bbox/jurisdiction matching, to avoid false positives. Classified SECONDARY, not MVP: real and valuable as a defense-in-depth check for any unincorporated-county road crossings the route may have (not yet fully enumerated against the GPX), but not expected to be the primary signal for the incorporated-city segments where KC-01/02/03/SAM-01/ISS-01 already carry MVP-grade coverage.

sources.research_notes: NEW SOURCE, added and directly live-tested in the fourth follow-up cycle (2026-07-28), found alongside KC-06 in the same RoadAlerts folder of King County's ArcGIS Server. The MapServer's own service description states it is 'primarily intended to be used by the King County MyCommute web site' - i.e. this is the backend feed for a public commute-conditions map, a strong signal it is a real, intentionally-public operational service. Layer list confirmed: DuvallRoadAlerts (point/line), TukwilaRoadAlerts (point/line), SammamishRoadAlerts (point/line), SeaTacRoadAlerts (point/line) - eight layers, four participating cities. Directly queried SammamishRoadAlerts_line (layer 5), the one layer relevant to this route: returned a valid schema (AlertTitle/AlertDescription/ClosureStatus/AlertStartDate/AlertEndDate/AlertURL/CreatedDate/ModifiedDate) confirming the service is structurally real and closure-status-capable - genuinely better-suited in principle to route-impact detection than any free-text HTML source in this registry, since it has explicit status/date/URL fields rather than requiring prose parsing. HOWEVER: the only record present is AlertID 1, AlertTitle 'Test', AlertDescription 'Thisd is only as test' [sic], AlertURL pointing to sammamish.us's homepage, dated 2014-09-05 - a stale placeholder/test record, not live content. Classified UNRESOLVED rather than REJECT or SECONDARY: the schema and mechanism are real and verified, but there is no evidence this layer is actively populated with real alerts today, nor evidence it has been abandoned - it may simply be that Sammamish has had no MyCommute-reportable road alert recently, or that this specific jurisdiction's feed was never fully adopted after initial setup. A future cycle should query this endpoint again after some elapsed time to see if the record count or content ever changes from this single 2014 test entry before deciding whether to REJECT (abandoned) or upgrade to SECONDARY/MVP (confirmed live). Also note: this service does NOT cover Redmond, Kenmore, Bothell, Woodinville, or Issaquah, so it cannot replace KC-01/02/03/SAM-01/ISS-01 for those segments even if fully live.

sources.research_notes: REJECTED as an acquisition source, sixth follow-up cycle (2026-07-29): the project owner confirmed GovDelivery is not accessible to them, closing off both remaining paths to resolve the topic ID (a live subscribe flow with a monitored email, or a direct King County Parks staff inquiry conducted by the project owner). With no path to an automatable topic-scoped feed URL, and given that KC-01/02/03 already provide direct, official coverage of the same trail segments this source would have supplemented, continuing to carry OTH-02 as an open SECONDARY action item is no longer useful. Downgraded from SECONDARY/PARTIALLY_VERIFIED to REJECT/BLOCKED. The real, on-topic bulletin content confirmed in prior cycles (see below) remains true and is preserved here for the record, but this source is now closed rather than pending. RETESTED 2026-07-28 (follow-up cycle) with real, positive progress. Directly fetched two individual GovDelivery WAKING bulletin pages found via WebSearch: bulletin 2068179, 'Regional Trail Alert: Sammamish River Trail Closure in Woodinville 8/20-31', and bulletin 3b3827b, 'Update: New dates for construction work on Sammamish River Trail in Bothell' - both real, both directly relevant to this route's Sammamish River Trail - Bothell/Woodinville segment. This UPGRADES the source from BLOCKED (assumed dead-end) to PARTIALLY_VERIFIED: the underlying content stream is confirmed real, active, official (King County Parks via GovDelivery/Granicus), and on-topic, not merely a documented API pattern. HOWEVER, the specific subscribable topic ID for 'Regional Trail Alert'-class bulletins was still NOT identified this cycle: the subscriber signup page (public.govdelivery.com/accounts/WAKING/subscriber/new) only exposes the topic checklist AFTER a real email address is entered into the interactive form - a genuine access limitation for an automated research fetch, not a search-effort shortfall. THIRD FOLLOW-UP CYCLE (2026-07-28): probed the topic-ID question from three additional angles, all confirming the same genuine dead end without fabricating an ID: (1) WebSearch found more real 'Regional Trail Alert' bulletins (bulletin 24231fe, 'Closure on the Burke-Gilman Trail May 6'; bulletin 2d9c7c0, 'Portion of the East Lake Sammamish Trail closed beginning June 1' - a 2026-dated match confirming KC-03's closure independently through a third channel), further confirming the content stream but not a topic ID. (2) Directly fetched a numbered signup URL discovered via search, public.govdelivery.com/accounts/WAKING/signup/46599, hoping the numeric ID would map to a named topic; it rendered only the generic subscriber form (Email/SMS, Facebook/Google sign-in) with no topic name or ID exposed in the page content. (3) Fetched individual bulletin pages themselves (e.g. bulletin 2d9c7c0) checking for an in-page 'Sent under topic: X' label or per-topic subscribe link; none was found - only a generic 'Update your preferences or unsubscribe' link. (4) Fetched GovDelivery's own developer API documentation for the Topics endpoint, which confirms topic listing is an authenticated API operation only ('List all Topics' requires API credentials) with no documented public/unauthenticated enumeration method. CONCLUSION: the topic ID remains genuinely unresolved after two full research cycles and four independent discovery angles. This is a structural limitation of the GovDelivery platform as configured for this account, not a research gap that more searching would close. The general https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/WAKING/bulletins.rss endpoint was not retested this cycle (previously HTTP 406) and remains presumed blocked. Recommendation stays SECONDARY on the strength of confirmed real, relevant content; remains below MVP because no automatable topic-scoped feed URL was confirmed. The only remaining path is a human operator completing the GovDelivery subscribe flow with a real monitored email to reveal the topic checklist, or a direct phone/email inquiry to King County Parks communications staff requesting the topic ID or a working per-topic RSS URL directly.
